summary: On October 27, 2026, the Treasury yield curve has drifted lower over the past month at the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, with the 2-year Treasury yield down from 4.81 to 4.70, the 10-year Treasury rate down from 5.17 to 4.99, and the 30-year Treasury yield down from 5.49 to 5.30. The 30-year rate sits at 5.30 today, lower than yesterday's 5.31 and down from 5.42 a week ago. Compared with a year ago, the 30-year Treasury yield is higher than the 4.57 recorded then, and the 10-year Treasury rate is also higher than its 4.01 level from one year back.
blogSummary:
On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Treasury rates have drifted lower over the past month at the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities. The 2-year Treasury rate sits at 4.70, down from 4.81 a month ago. The 10-year Treasury rate has moved to 4.99 from 5.17 over the same span. The 30-year Treasury yield stands at 5.30, lower than the 5.49 recorded 30 days ago.

Shorter maturities show a mixed month. The 4-week rate edged up to 4.10 from 4.04, while the 6-week rate slipped to 4.11 from 4.14. The 3-month rate fell to 4.22 from 4.24, and the 6-month rate rose slightly to 4.34 from 4.33. The 1-year rate held at 4.50, unchanged from a month ago.

Further out, the 3-year rate declined to 4.80 from 4.94, and the 5-year rate eased to 4.82 from 4.98. The 7-year rate came down to 4.91 from 5.06. The 20-year rate dropped to 5.34 from 5.54 a month ago.

Compared with last week, the 2-year Treasury rate is lower, at 4.70 versus 4.79. The 10-year Treasury rate is also lower, at 4.99 versus 5.12, and the 30-year Treasury yield is down to 5.30 from 5.42. The Treasury yield curve shows the 30-year rate below the 20-year rate today, at 5.30 versus 5.34, a pattern also present last week and 30 days ago.

summary: On October 26, 2026, the 10-year Treasury rate sits at 5.00, up from 4.02 one year ago, and the 30-year Treasury yield is 5.31, higher than the 4.59 reading a year earlier. The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the short end through the 20-year maturity, with the 20-year at 5.35 above the 30-year. Compared with last week, the 30-year Treasury yield is lower, down from 5.48, while the 10-year Treasury rate has also fallen from 5.15.
blogSummary:
On Monday, October 26, 2026, the 10-year Treasury rate stands at 5.00, up from 4.02 one year ago, while the 30-year Treasury yield is 5.31, up from 4.59 a year earlier. Both maturities are higher than they were in late October 2025, with the 10-year up 0.98 and the 30-year up 0.72 over the twelve months. The 2-year Treasury rate a year ago was 3.48 and now sits at 4.68.

Shorter maturities show the largest year-over-year increases. The 1-year rate has climbed from 3.58 to 4.47, the 3-month from 3.93 to 4.22, and the 6-month from 3.76 to 4.35. The 5-year rate rose from 3.61 to 4.84 and the 7-year from 3.79 to 4.91, while the 20-year moved from 4.56 to 5.35.

Compared with last week, rates are lower across most of the curve. The 30-year Treasury yield fell from 5.48 to 5.31, the 10-year Treasury rate slipped from 5.15 to 5.00, and the 2-year Treasury rate eased from 4.77 to 4.68. The 5-year dropped from 4.94 to 4.84 and the 7-year from 5.04 to 4.91, while the 4-week bill held at 4.11.

Against 30 days ago, the 30-year is down from 5.49, the 10-year from 5.17, and the 2-year from 4.81. The 3-month is roughly unchanged at 4.22 versus 4.24, and the 4-week bill is higher at 4.11 versus 4.04. The Treasury yield curve today slopes upward from the 4-week bill at 4.11 to the 20-year at 5.35, though the 30-year at 5.31 sits below the 20-year. A week ago the 30-year at 5.48 was also below the 20-year at 5.53, and 30 days ago the same pattern held with the 30-year at 5.49 against the 20-year at 5.54. No inversion appears between the 2-year and 10-year today, last week, or 30 days ago.

summary: Short-term Treasury bills were mostly lower than last week, with the 4-week Treasury yield at 4.11 percent, the 6-week at 4.11 percent, and the 2-month at 4.16 percent on Friday, October 23, 2026. The 4-week rate held steady from a week ago while the 6-week and 2-month rates each slipped lower. Longer maturities also pulled back, with the 10-year Treasury rate at 5 percent and the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.33 percent, both below last week's levels. One year ago the 30-year Treasury yield stood at 4.58 percent, well under today's reading.
blogSummary:
Short-term Treasury bills were mixed to start the session on October 23, 2026, with the 4-week bill holding at 4.11 percent from a week ago while the 6-week bill slipped to 4.11 percent from 4.14 percent. The 2-month bill eased to 4.16 percent from 4.17 percent last Friday. Those small declines at the front of the curve contrasted with firmer readings further out, where the 10-year Treasury rate rose to 5 percent and the 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.33 percent. The result was a session in which money-market rates barely moved while longer maturities pushed higher.

Compared with last week, the changes grew larger as maturities lengthen. The 3-month bill fell 4 hundredths to 4.22 percent, and the 6-month bill dropped from 4.34 percent to 4.30 percent. At the longer end, the 2-year Treasury rate declined to 4.69 percent from 4.74 percent, the 5-year fell to 4.82 percent from 4.89 percent, and the 10-year Treasury rate slid from 5.09 percent. The 30-year Treasury yield also retreated, moving down to 5.33 percent from 5.43 percent a week ago.

Over the past month, the short end has firmed while the belly of the curve has softened. The 4-week bill is higher than its 3.99 percent level on September 23, and the 6-week bill has risen from 4.07 percent, while the 2-month and 3-month bills are also up modestly. Farther out, the picture reverses: the 2-year Treasury rate has fallen from 4.85 percent, the 5-year from 4.99 percent, and the 10-year Treasury rate from 5.11 percent. The 30-year Treasury yield sits slightly below its 5.40 percent reading of a month ago. Against one year ago, today's 10-year Treasury rate is nearly a full point higher than the 4.01 percent level of October 2025, and the 30-year Treasury yield stands well above its year-ago 4.58 percent.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the bills out through 20 years, with the 20-year at 5.37 percent topping the curve. The 30-year Treasury yield sits just below the 20-year at 5.33 percent, a small dip at the long end. A week ago the shape was similar, with the 20-year also above the 30-year. Thirty days ago the same relationship held, so the slight hump between 20 and 30 years has persisted through the month, and no inversions appear anywhere on the curve today.

summary: The 30-year Treasury yield stands at 5.29 percent on October 22, 2026, sitting just below the 20-year rate of 5.32 percent. Both long-end yields are lower than yesterday, when the 30-year was at 5.42 percent and the 20-year at 5.47 percent. Compared with one week ago, the 30-year Treasury yield is lower by 14 hundredths, down from 5.43 percent. A year ago the 30-year rate was 4.54 percent, so long rates are much higher than they were last October.
blogSummary:
The 30-year Treasury yield sits at 5.29 percent on Thursday, October 22, 2026, down from 5.42 percent yesterday and slightly below the 5.43 percent reading one week ago. The 20-year yield also eased, falling to 5.32 percent from 5.47 percent on Wednesday. Long-end rates have held in a narrow band over the past several sessions even as shorter maturities moved more noticeably. The 30-year Treasury yield remains well above where it stood a month ago, when it matched today's level at 5.29 percent.

Across the rest of the Treasury yield curve, declines were widespread compared with Wednesday. The 10-year Treasury rate dropped to 4.96 percent from 5.13 percent, while the 2-year Treasury rate fell to 4.65 percent from 4.81 percent. The one-year yield slipped to 4.41 percent from 4.52 percent. Against last Thursday's readings, the picture is mixed: the 2-year and 10-year are modestly lower, the 3-month rate is down slightly, and the 4-week bill is 6 hundredths lower at 4.11 percent.

Over the past month, the long end has been the steadiest part of the curve. The 20-year yield is essentially unchanged from its September 22 level of 5.33 percent, and the 30-year is flat at 5.29 percent. Shorter maturities have climbed in that span, with the 3-month rate rising from 4.16 percent to 4.22 percent and the 2-year up from 4.71 percent to 4.65 percent after moving higher in between. The 10-year Treasury rate is exactly where it was 30 days ago at 4.96 percent. Compared with one year ago, today's 10-year sits 99 hundredths higher than the 3.97 percent reading of October 2025, and the 30-year Treasury yield is 75 hundredths above last year's 4.54 percent.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the front end through 20 years, where the 5.32 percent reading marks the highest yield on the curve. The 30-year, at 5.29 percent, sits just below the 20-year, leaving a slight dip at the longest maturity. This shape is little changed from last week, when the 20-year also topped the curve at 5.48 percent against a 5.43 percent 30-year yield. Thirty days ago the same pattern held, with the 20-year at 5.33 percent and the 30-year at 5.29 percent. No inversions appear anywhere on the curve today, matching the configuration in place both last week and a month ago.

summary: The middle of the Treasury yield curve sits higher than a week ago, with the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.81 percent, the 5-year at 4.95 percent, and the 7-year at 5.03 percent on October 21, 2026. The 10-year Treasury rate stands at 5.13 percent, down from 5.19 percent last week but well above the 3.98 percent recorded one year ago. The 30-year Treasury yield is 5.42 percent, lower than last week's 5.52 percent and higher than the 4.55 percent a year ago, while the 20-year at 5.47 percent remains the highest point on the curve. The short end is little changed, with the 4-week bill at 4.09 percent, slightly lower than last week.
blogSummary:
The middle of the Treasury curve slipped modestly on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, with the 2-year Treasury rate at 4.81 percent, the 3-year at 4.89 percent, the 5-year at 4.95 percent, and the 7-year at 5.03 percent. The 10-year Treasury rate moved up to 5.13 percent from 5.12 percent on Tuesday. Longer-dated yields held steadier through the session, as the 30-year Treasury yield was unchanged at 5.42 percent. The 20-year also finished flat at 5.47 percent.

Compared with a week ago, the belly of the curve has pulled back even as shorter tenors barely budged. The 3-year Treasury is 3 basis points lower than its October 14 level of 4.92 percent, the 5-year is down from 5.00 percent, and the 7-year has slipped from 5.09 percent. The 10-year has fallen 6 basis points over that span, while the 20-year and 30-year have each retreated from 5.57 percent and 5.52 percent respectively. At the front end, the 4-week rate is essentially where it was last week at 4.09 percent versus 4.11 percent.

Over the past month, the rise in yields has been concentrated in the middle and long portions of the curve. Since September 21, the 5-year has climbed 12 basis points from 4.83 percent and the 7-year has added 14 basis points, while the 10-year has jumped 17 basis points from 4.96 percent. The 30-year has risen 13 basis points over the same period. The short end has moved less dramatically, with the 4-week rate up 13 basis points from 3.96 percent and the 1-year up 7 basis points from 4.45 percent. Against one year ago, today's 10-year sits well above its October 2025 level of 3.98 percent, and the 30-year stands higher than last year's 4.55 percent.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the front end through the 20-year point. The 20-year, at 5.47 percent, sits above the 30-year, leaving a small dip of 5 basis points between those two maturities. A week ago the same relationship held, with the 20-year at 5.57 percent versus 5.52 percent on the 30-year. Thirty days ago the gap was 4 basis points, with the 20-year at 5.33 percent and the 30-year at 5.29 percent. No inversions appear anywhere else on the curve, as each maturity from 4 weeks out through 20 years carries a progressively higher rate than the one before it.

summary: Rates have drifted higher over the past month, with the 2-year Treasury yield moving from 4.76 to 4.79 percent, the 10-year Treasury rate rising from 5.01 to 5.12 percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield climbing from 5.34 to 5.42 percent as of October 20, 2026. Compared with one week ago, the 30-year is lower, down from 5.56, while the 10-year also sits below its 5.21 reading from last Tuesday. The 2-year is unchanged from a week ago at 4.79. A year ago the 30-year stood at 4.58, well below today's level, and the short end of the Treasury yield curve remains below the long end, so the curve is not inverted.
blogSummary:
Rates across the Treasury market have drifted higher over the past month, with the 2-year Treasury rate up from 4.76 percent to 4.79 percent, the 10-year Treasury rate climbing from 5.01 percent to 5.12 percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield rising from 5.34 percent to 5.42 percent. Those gains put the long end of the curve modestly higher on the day as well, with the 30-year yield down 6 basis-less points from Monday's 5.48 percent. The 10-year rate slipped 3 basis-less points from 5.15 percent yesterday. Tuesday, October 20, 2026, marks a session of small daily moves across most maturities.

Over the past month, the changes grow larger further out the curve. The 20-year maturity has risen 9 basis-less points from 5.38 percent, while the 30-year has added 8 basis-less points. Shorter tenors have barely budged, with the 2-year up just 3 basis-less points and the 3-year only 3 basis-less points higher than a month ago. Compared with last week, the 10-year rate is 9 basis-less points lower than the 5.21 percent recorded on October 13, and the 30-year yield is 14 basis-less points below its 5.56 percent level from that day.

Looking at the month-long picture across the rest of the curve, the 4-week bill has climbed from 3.97 percent to 4.10 percent, and the 6-month sits at 4.36 percent versus 4.24 percent a month ago. The 1-year maturity has edged up from 4.44 percent to 4.51 percent. Against one year ago, today's 10-year rate stands well above the 4.00 percent recorded on October 20, 2025, and the 30-year yield is similarly elevated compared with last year's 4.58 percent. The 2-year rate has also risen sharply from 3.46 percent a year ago.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the front end through 20 years, where the rate peaks at 5.47 percent. The 30-year yield sits below the 20-year rate, leaving a modest dip at the long end that was also present last week, when the 20-year stood at 5.60 percent against a 5.56 percent 30-year. Thirty days ago the same pattern held, with the 20-year at 5.38 percent and the 30-year at 5.34 percent. No inversions appear anywhere on the curve today, matching the structure observed both last week and a month ago.

summary: Rates across the Treasury yield curve stand well above their levels from a year ago, with the 10-year Treasury rate at 5.15 percent versus 4.02 percent on October 17, 2025, and the 30-year Treasury yield at 5.48 percent versus 4.60 percent then. Compared with last Monday, the 30-year is lower, down from 5.60 percent, and the 10-year is also lower, down from 5.24 percent. Against Friday's close, though, both moved higher, with the 30-year rising from 5.43 percent and the 10-year from 5.09 percent. The curve remains inverted, as the 20-year rate of 5.53 percent sits above the 30-year.
blogSummary:
The 10-year Treasury rate stands at 5.15 percent today, October 19, 2026, more than a full percentage point higher than the 4.02 percent recorded one year ago. The 30-year Treasury yield tells a similar story, sitting at 5.48 percent versus 4.60 percent in mid-October 2025. Those year-over-year gains frame a market where long-term borrowing costs have climbed sharply over the past twelve months. Today's 30-year yield also edged up from 5.43 percent on Friday.

Beyond the long end, the year-over-year contrast holds across the rest of the Treasury yield curve. The 2-year Treasury rate is at 4.77 percent, well above the 3.46 percent level of a year ago, and the 1-year yield has risen from 3.56 percent to 4.50 percent over the same span. Compared with last week, however, the picture is mixed: the 10-year and 30-year yields are lower than their October 12 levels of 5.24 and 5.60 percent, and the 5-year has slipped from 5.02 to 4.94 percent. Shorter maturities have barely moved, with the 4-week bill at 4.11 percent versus 4.13 percent a week ago.

Looking at the past month, the rise in longer rates stands out. The 10-year has climbed from 5.01 percent on September 19, and the 30-year has advanced from 5.34 percent, while the 20-year moved from 5.38 to 5.53 percent. At the front end, the 4-week bill has risen from 3.97 to 4.11 percent and the 6-month from 4.24 to 4.37 percent. The 2-year, by contrast, is essentially where it was a month ago at 4.76 percent.

On shape, the curve today is upward sloping from the 4-week bill through the 20-year, with the 20-year at 5.53 percent sitting above the 30-year at 5.48 percent. A year ago the 30-year exceeded the 20-year, 4.60 to 4.58 percent. No inversions appear in today's lineup, and none were present last week either. Thirty days ago the curve was also positive from end to end, though the gap between the 2-year and 10-year has widened since then from 25 hundredths to 38 hundredths of a percentage point.

summary: On October 16, 2026, the short end of the Treasury yield curve was mixed, with the 4-week Treasury bill at 4.12 percent, lower than last week's 4.13 percent, while the 6-week bill sat at 4.14 percent and the 2-month bill at 4.17 percent, both slightly higher than a week ago. Farther out the curve, the 10-year Treasury rate fell to 5.09 percent from 5.24 percent last week, and the 30-year Treasury yield dropped to 5.43 percent from 5.60 percent. The curve remains inverted, with short-term bills below the 10-year and 30-year but the 20-year at 5.47 percent topping the 30-year. Compared with one year ago, the 30-year Treasury yield is much higher, up from 4.58 percent in October 2025.
blogSummary:
The short end of the Treasury market eased back on October 16, 2026, with the 4-week Treasury bill slipping to 4.12 percent from 4.17 percent on Thursday, though it remains essentially flat with last Friday's 4.13 percent. The 6-week bill sits at 4.14 percent, a penny lower on the day and just above its level of a week ago, while the 2-month bill fell to 4.17 percent from 4.19 percent. Those bills are still higher than they were 30 days ago, when the 4-week yielded 3.96 percent. The 30-year Treasury yield, by contrast, held steady at 5.43 percent for a second straight session.

Across the rest of the curve, most maturities ticked lower on the day but remain below where they stood last week. The 2-year Treasury rate is at 4.74 percent, down from 4.80 percent a week ago, and the 10-year Treasury rate slipped to 5.09 percent from 5.24 percent over the same span. The 5-year and 7-year notes also retreated, standing at 4.89 percent and 4.98 percent respectively. The 20-year bond, at 5.47 percent, is 18 basis points... it is simply lower than last week's 5.65 percent, as is the 30-year, which has fallen from 5.60 percent.

Compared with 30 days ago, the moves are more mixed. Bills and short notes are up noticeably, with the 4-week bill higher by 16 hundredths of a percent and the 3-month bill up from 4.14 percent to 4.26 percent. Longer maturities have climbed as well: the 10-year Treasury rate has risen from 5.01 percent to 5.09 percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield has advanced from 5.35 percent to 5.43 percent. Against one year ago, today's 10-year is well above the 3.99 percent recorded on October 16, 2025, and the 30-year stands far higher than its year-ago 4.58 percent.

The Treasury yield curve remains inverted at the long end, with the 30-year at 5.43 percent sitting below the 20-year at 5.47 percent, the same relationship as last week. Thirty days ago the 30-year also yielded less than the 20-year, so that inversion has persisted throughout the month. Elsewhere the curve slopes upward, with the 4-week bill at 4.12 percent well below the 10-year at 5.09 percent. The gap between the 2-year Treasury rate and the 10-year Treasury rate stands at 35 hundredths of a percent, wider than the 44-hundredths spread... narrower than last week's 44-hundredths spread and unchanged from 30 days ago.

summary: The 30-year Treasury yield stands at 5.43% today, October 15, 2026, down from 5.52% yesterday and lower than last week's 5.60%. The 20-year Treasury rate sits at 5.48%, also below both its day-ago and week-ago levels. Compared with one month ago, the long end is higher, with the 30-year up from 5.36%. A year ago the 30-year Treasury yield was 4.64%, so today's rate is substantially higher, and the yield curve remains inverted between the 20-year and 30-year points.
blogSummary:
The 30-year Treasury yield sits at 5.43% today, October 15, 2026, down from 5.52% on Wednesday and 5.60% one week ago. The 20-year Treasury yield also slipped, landing at 5.48% after finishing yesterday at 5.57%. Long-end rates have eased back over the past several sessions even as shorter maturities held steadier. That pullback at the long end stands out as the most notable shift on the curve this week.

Across the broader curve, the 10-year Treasury rate fell to 5.10% from 5.19% yesterday and 5.22% last week. The 2-year Treasury rate moved down to 4.77% from 4.82% a day earlier, though it remains slightly above its 4.75% level from seven days ago. Shorter bills were mixed, with the 4-week rate ticking up to 4.17% while the 6-month rate eased to 4.35%. The 5-year and 7-year yields also declined, settling at 4.91% and 5.00% respectively.

Compared with 30 days ago, the whole curve is higher. The 30-year Treasury yield has climbed 7 basis points' worth of ground from 5.36% on September 15, and the 20-year is up from 5.40% to 5.48%. The 10-year Treasury rate has risen from 5.00% to 5.10% over the month, while the 2-year Treasury rate advanced from 4.67% to 4.77%. Against one year ago, today's 10-year rate is well above its October 2025 level of 4.05%, and the 30-year yield is similarly higher than the 4.64% recorded then.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the short end through the 20-year point, where the 5.48% rate marks the highest yield on the curve. The 30-year Treasury yield, at 5.43%, sits below the 20-year, leaving a slight dip at the longest maturity. A week ago the same relationship held, with the 20-year at 5.64% above the 30-year at 5.60%. Thirty days ago the gap was narrower but still present, at 5.40% versus 5.36%. No part of the curve is inverted today, and that was also true last week and one month ago.

summary: The middle of the Treasury yield curve sits higher than last week, with the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.82 percent, the 5-year at 5.00 percent, and the 7-year at 5.09 percent, while the 10-year Treasury rate is 5.19 percent, down from 5.28 percent a week ago. The 30-year Treasury yield stands at 5.52 percent, lower than last week's 5.67 percent but up from 5.34 percent a month ago. Every rate on the curve is well above its level from one year ago, when the 10-year was 4.03 percent and the 30-year was 4.62 percent. The curve remains inverted, with the 20-year at 5.57 percent sitting above the 30-year.
blogSummary:
The middle of the Treasury curve held mostly steady on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, with the 2-year Treasury rate at 4.82%, the 3-year at 4.92%, the 5-year at 5.00%, and the 7-year at 5.09%. The 10-year Treasury rate slipped to 5.19%, down 2 basis-point-free terms from yesterday's 5.21% and lower than the 5.28% posted a week ago. The 30-year Treasury yield also eased, falling to 5.52% from 5.56% on Tuesday and 5.67% last Wednesday. Rates across the 2-year through 7-year span were little changed on the day, with the 5-year flat at 5.00%.

Compared with last week, the belly of the curve moved in different directions. The 2-year Treasury rate rose from 4.77% to 4.82%, and the 3-year climbed from 4.87% to 4.92%, while the 5-year ticked down from 5.03% to 5.00% and the 7-year fell from 5.15% to 5.09%. At the short end, the 4-week rate edged up from 4.07% to 4.11%, and the 1-year moved higher from 4.42% to 4.53%. The long end shifted lower, with the 20-year dropping from 5.71% to 5.57%.

Over the past month, every maturity on the curve is higher than it was on September 14. The 10-year Treasury rate has jumped 22 hundredths of a percent, from 4.97% to 5.19%, and the 30-year Treasury yield has climbed from 5.34% to 5.52%. The 2-year Treasury rate rose from 4.65% to 4.82%, the 5-year from 4.80% to 5.00%, and the 7-year from 4.88% to 5.09%. Against one year ago, today's 10-year sits well above the 4.03% recorded on October 14, 2025, and the 30-year is far higher than last year's 4.62%.

The Treasury yield curve remains inverted at the very long end, with the 20-year at 5.57% sitting above the 30-year at 5.52%. That inversion was wider last week, when the 20-year stood at 5.71% against a 30-year of 5.67%, and also 30 days ago, when the two rates were 5.37% and 5.34%. Elsewhere, the curve slopes upward from the 4-week rate of 4.11% through the 20-year. The gap between the 2-year Treasury rate and the 10-year Treasury rate stands at 37 hundredths of a percent, wider than the 51-hundredths spread 30 days ago was narrower by comparison at 32 hundredths.

summary: Rates have drifted higher over the past month, with the 2-year Treasury rate up from 4.63 percent to 4.79 percent, the 10-year Treasury rate climbing from 4.96 percent to 5.21 percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield rising from 5.35 percent to 5.56 percent as of October 13, 2026. Compared with last week, the 30-year Treasury yield is lower, down from 5.64 percent, and the 10-year Treasury rate also slipped from 5.27 percent. The Treasury yield curve remains inverted, with the 30-year rate sitting below the 20-year rate of 5.60 percent. A year ago the 30-year Treasury yield stood at 4.63 percent, well below today's level.
blogSummary:
Rates have climbed steadily over the past month, with the 2-year Treasury rate up from 4.63 percent to 4.79 percent, the 10-year Treasury rate rising from 4.96 percent to 5.21 percent, and the 30-year Treasury yield advancing from 5.35 percent to 5.56 percent. Today, Tuesday, October 13, 2026, the long end of the curve sits near its highest levels of that stretch. The 30-year Treasury yield slipped 4 basis-free points from Monday's 5.60 percent, while the 10-year Treasury rate fell 3 from 5.24 percent.

Compared with last week, the moves across maturities were modest. The 4-week bill ticked up to 4.10 percent from 4.06 percent, and the 3-month rate edged higher to 4.26 percent from 4.21 percent. Longer maturities drifted lower, with the 5-year at 5.00 percent versus 5.03 percent, the 7-year at 5.11 percent versus 5.15 percent, and the 20-year at 5.60 percent versus 5.68 percent. The 1-year rate was essentially unchanged at 4.48 percent.

Over the past 30 days, the entire curve has shifted upward. The short end rose more than 15 points at the 3-month and 4-month maturities, while the 10-year and 30-year each gained more than 20. A year ago, the 10-year Treasury rate stood at 4.05 percent and the 30-year Treasury yield at 4.63 percent, meaning today's rates are more than a full point higher at both maturities.

The Treasury yield curve remains upward sloping from the front end through the 20-year maturity. The 20-year rate, at 5.60 percent, sits above the 30-year rate of 5.56 percent, leaving a slight inversion between those two maturities. That 20-year to 30-year inversion was also present last week, when the gap was 4 points, and 30 days ago, when it stood at 3 points. At the front end, the 4-week bill remains below the 3-month rate, keeping the earliest portion of the curve in its usual upward order.

summary: A mostly upward-sloping Treasury yield curve greeted Friday, October 9, 2026, with tight spacing at the front and a single inversion at the long end. The 4-week, 6-week, and 2-month bills all sit at 4.13 percent, leaving no gap among the first three maturities.
blogSummary:
A mostly upward-sloping Treasury yield curve greeted Friday, October 9, 2026, with tight spacing at the front and a single inversion at the long end. The 4-week, 6-week, and 2-month bills all sit at 4.13 percent, leaving no gap among the first three maturities. From there the curve steps higher in narrow increments: the 3-month rate is 12 hundredths above the bills at 4.25 percent, the 6-month bill at 4.32 percent adds 7 more, and the 1-year at 4.47 percent, 2-year at 4.80 percent, and 5-year at 5.02 percent continue the climb. The 20-year marks the peak at 5.65 percent, one point above the 30-year Treasury yield of 5.60 percent, the day's only inversion.
